ratings_why.fun: The drain turn, where a saved Purse floods every Fanfare at once, is a real payoff moment, and each card reads in one line once the town is printed; the fights are still mostly +1/+1 piles.
ratings_why.distinct: Two rival gold counters on one tribe is fresh and the fable plays itself, but holding gold overlaps Hedgerow's Larder, which keeps it from an 8.

verdict_why: v2 fixed the town reading; what's left is wording polish and balance, which more rounds would only shuffle.

points.text: Tymbal Drummer and Maestro Tettix say 'gold you spent this Recruit Phase / this turn'; saying 'your Spent' would tie them to the counter the player is already watching.
Lord Fennimore's line about Tithonus is a rules reminder inside card text; move it to a tooltip so the card reads as one effect.
The woodland folk come through in the economy but not in the fight; one Hive fight trick, like the Winter Cluster swap already in risks, would let the board look like bees on screen.
Lantern Seller and Bandstand Horn are the two cards that could belong to any tribe; a Carnival flavour such as moulted shells or a procession order would make them read as cicadas.

standouts.why: Winter Cluster turns savings into front-row Health: one glance, and it is the bees' winter cluster.
The Borrower is the cicada at the ant's door: free gold if you end broke, a tax if you save, and a placement puzzle.
Ottavia asks for balanced books with one simple number, the smaller of the two.

weakest.why: Lantern Seller is a plain gold refund with no festival in what it does.
Bandstand Horn is a generic random +1/+1 spread.
Root Nymph's two tiny triggers don't show the long wait underground the nymph stands for.

flags.note: Mother Melissa doubling Old Messor and Granary Clerk on a big float could run away late.
Madame Cigale on a full drain turn pays 10-20 times across the board.
Lord Fennimore stacked with Tithonus needs the shown numbers on the cards ('3/6'), or players will miscount.
